research_question: Under the specified conditions, does the distribution of five-minute fixed-location temperature-drop scores differ between continuous lower-speed stirring and intermittent higher-speed stirring?

landscape.summary: A synthetic procedural specification defines two paddle-stirring methods for comparing five-minute fixed-location temperature-drop scores in 100 mL water. Method A commands continuous clockwise 30 rpm from time zero to 300 s; Method B commands clockwise 60 rpm during five nominal 30-s active intervals and stop outside those intervals. The comparison combines differences in commanded speed and stirring schedule, including uninterrupted stirring duration, and therefore does not isolate intermittency alone. The score is S = T0 − T300, using the recorded temperatures at 0.1 °C resolution. No experimental results or observed values are reported, the distributional comparison remains unresolved, and no scientific superiority is established. Interpretation must retain limitations concerning physical adherence, measurement performance and dependence across runs.
landscape.uncertainty: The source-defined specifications are design choices; they do not establish empirical conformity or effects. Command logs and rated motor performance do not verify actual motion, and the proposed two-temperature reference check evaluates only limited agreement under its check conditions. Fresh aliquots alone do not establish independence when apparatus, sessions or preparations are shared. Allocation, run order, replication and confounding control remain human decisions unspecified by the source, which supplies no sample-size justification or results.

items.text: Method A is specified as continuous clockwise paddle stirring at a commanded 30 rpm throughout the nominal interval from time zero to 300 s, with the paddle remaining immersed and not repositioned. Method B commands clockwise 60 rpm during the five nominal active intervals [0,30), [60,90), [120,150), [180,210) and [240,270), and commands stop outside those active intervals, including [270,300], with the paddle remaining immersed and in the same position throughout. These are commanded schedules, not observations establishing actual speed, physical stopping, transition duration or revolution totals. Command logs and rated motor performance do not themselves measure actual speed, transition duration or revolution totals; without suitable existing feedback, some physical adherence requirements may remain unverified. No equality of mechanical work or energy input follows from nominal rotation totals.

items.text: Score S = T0 − T300 uses the recorded temperatures at 0.1 °C resolution without additional transformation, normalization, absolute-value conversion, clipping or averaging. Both inputs must be finite and within 0–60 °C, with T0 additionally meeting its starting-temperature requirement; for a valid T0, S lies between T0 − 60 and T0 as input-validity bounds, not physical predictions. If either endpoint is absent, non-finite, outside its stated range or outside its timing allowance, no valid score is available; interpolation, substitution of another timestamp and imputation are prohibited. The defined construct is five-minute temperature drop at the fixed probe location, not a direct measure of total heat lost, energy efficiency or uniform bulk-water temperature. A larger recorded drop does not automatically designate a scientifically superior method. Endpoint validity, reference-check eligibility and method-adherence status must remain distinct.
items.uncertainty: The score rule and validity bounds define the operational measure, while empirical measurement performance remains uncertain. A numerically valid score alone does not establish instrument eligibility or method conformity.

items.text: T0 must be within 44.8–45.2 °C and recorded within 10 s of vessel removal from the warming bath while the paddle is stationary; that recording defines time zero. The probe tip is specified 15 ± 1 mm above the internal base and 20 ± 1 mm horizontally from the shaft axis, without touching the vessel or paddle. The probe/logger requirements are 0.1 °C reporting resolution, rated accuracy no worse than ±0.2 °C over 20–50 °C and rated 90% response time no longer than 5 s; these are specified ratings, not measured performance. The reference thermometer requires resolution of 0.1 °C or finer, documented accuracy no worse than ±0.1 °C over 20–50 °C and a dated calibration or verification record providing a documented basis for current suitability; display resolution alone is insufficient. The proposed reference check uses the task’s probe/logger configuration and the reference thermometer in well-mixed water, with sensing tips adjacent and no more than 5 mm apart, without contact with each other or the container. At each reference-temperature band, 21–23 °C and 44–46 °C, after readings settle, three paired probe/reference readings must be recorded approximately 5 s apart, spanning 10 s. Every reference reading must fall within its band, and the reference range and probe range across the three readings must each be no greater than 0.1 °C. The proposed acceptance criterion requires |probe reading − reference reading| ≤ 0.2 °C for every paired reading at both bands, with both bands satisfying the temperature-band, stability and agreement criteria. This check evaluates limited agreement under its check conditions; it does not establish absolute accuracy, response behavior during stirring, complete-range performance or measurement reliability across repeated runs. The source supplies no certificate, calibration result or verified instrument performance, and no instrument is shown to have passed this proposed check.
items.uncertainty: Probe lag, calibration error, timestamp error, vessel thermal history, residual exterior moisture, ambient drift and water loss could affect recorded outcomes. Reference uncertainty and temperature differences between adjacent sensing tips remain relevant; specified ratings and a proposed agreement threshold do not resolve these limitations.

items.text: The experimental and observation unit is one fresh water aliquot undergoing one uninterrupted five-minute run with one stirring method; within-run temperature samples are repeated measurements of that unit, not independent experimental units or independent replicates. Fresh aliquots alone do not establish independence across runs: reused apparatus, runs in the same session or shared preparations may introduce dependence. For Method A, a 30-rpm setting is a command, and a display repeating it is not necessarily an actual-speed measurement; available feedback must be recorded as measured, controller-estimated or merely the commanded setting. In the cited Method A passage, the one-second physical transition allowance—from an issued start command to speed within ±2 rpm of target, or an issued stop command to a stationary paddle—is distinct from command-boundary timing. One allowance must not be reported as verification of the other; acceleration and deceleration mean physical motion need not coincide exactly with the nominal active interval.
items.uncertainty: The unit and Method A timing definitions are explicit, but neither statistical independence nor physical adherence follows from those definitions alone. Apparatus reuse, allocation, run order, replication and confounding control require human study-level decisions that the source does not supply.

evidence.source_text:
Check procedure: Use the task’s probe/logger configuration and the reference thermometer in
well-mixed water, with their sensing tips adjacent, no more than 5 mm apart, without contact with each
other or the container. Check two reference-temperature bands: 21–23 °C and 44–46 °C.
At each band, after readings have settled, record three paired probe/reference readings approximately
five seconds apart, spanning ten seconds. Each reference reading must fall within that band. Across the
three readings, the reference range and the probe range must each be no greater than 0.1 °C.
Proposed acceptance criterion: At both bands, every paired reading must satisfy:
|probe reading − reference reading| ≤ 0.2 °C.
Both bands must meet the temperature-band, stability, and agreement criteria.

Subtract without additional transformation,
normalization, absolute-value conversion, clipping, or averaging. Report S to one decimal place in
degrees Celsius of temperature difference.
Direction and interpretation: Positive S denotes a lower endpoint probe temperature; zero denotes no
change resolved by the recorded values; negative S denotes a higher endpoint probe temperature. A
larger score denotes a larger recorded temperature drop under these conditions. It does not
automatically designate a scientifically superior method.

Reference suitability: The reference thermometer must have reporting resolution of 0.1 °C or finer and
documented accuracy no worse than ±0.1 °C over 20–50 °C. Record its manufacturer/model, identifying
serial number or local instrument label, applicable accuracy specification, and current calibration or
verification status. A dated calibration or verification record must provide a documented basis for its
current suitability. Display resolution alone is insufficient.
Use only documentation that actually exists. This source supplies no certificate, calibration result, or
verified instrument performance.

Valid range: Both inputs must be finite and within 0–60 °C, and T0 must additionally meet the
starting-temperature requirement. Consequently, for a given valid T0, the numerical score lies between
T0 − 60 and T0. These are input-validity bounds, not predictions about physical behavior. Do not clamp
unexpected values into this range.
Measurement occasion: T0 is captured immediately before stirring begins. T300 is the scheduled
300-second sample, captured before Method A’s final stop command; Method B is already stationary.
Endpoint timestamps must be within one second of their scheduled occasions. Motor command
allowances do not shift the endpoint measurement occasion.

This is not a real empirical study. No experimental results or fictional experimental observations
are reported. All numerical settings below are proposed procedural specifications, not observed values.
This case is independent of earlier synthetic documents. Its Method A, Method B, task, and score are
newly defined here; they do not recover the meanings of labels in an earlier corpus. No institution,
publication, author identity, DOI, or research citation is asserted.

The methods also differ in instantaneous speed and uninterrupted stirring
duration, so a future comparison could not isolate “intermittency alone.”
Probe lag, calibration error, timestamp error, vessel thermal history, residual exterior moisture, ambient
drift, and water loss could affect the recorded outcome. Equal nominal rotations do not remove these
limitations.
The two-temperature reference check evaluates limited agreement under its check conditions. It does not
establish absolute accuracy, response behavior during stirring, complete-range performance, or
measurement reliability across repeated runs. Reference uncertainty and temperature differences
between adjacent sensing tips remain relevant.

Section 4 — Method B: Intermittent higher-speed paddle stirring
Method B is clockwise paddle stirring at a commanded speed of 60 revolutions per minute during these
five nominal active intervals, expressed in seconds after time zero:
[0, 30), [60, 90), [120, 150), [180, 210), and [240, 270).
The paddle is commanded to stop during all intervening intervals, including [270, 300]. It remains
immersed and in the same position throughout.
Method B independently requires the water, vessel, paddle, probe placement, preparation,
reference-check eligibility, and environment defined in Section 2. Initiate the first active interval
immediately after recording T0. Capture T300 while the paddle is stationary; issue no new stirring
command at 300 seconds.

Preparation and required actions: Fill the vessel with a fresh aliquot. With the stationary paddle and
probe immersed in their specified positions, condition the vessel in the warming bath until the probe
reads 45.0 ± 0.2 °C and changes by no more than 0.1 °C over ten seconds. Remove the vessel, dry its
exterior, and place it on the cork support.
Within ten seconds of removal, record the initial probe temperature as T0 while the paddle is stationary.
T0 must be within 44.8–45.2 °C. That recording defines time zero; immediately initiate the chosen stirring
schedule.

Repeated observations: Intermediate one-second samples preserve the temperature trace but do not
contribute to S. There is one score per run. Repeated runs retain separate scores; this document defines
no across-run aggregation.
Missing or invalid observations: If either endpoint is absent, non-finite, outside the stated range, or
outside its timing allowance, no valid score is available. Do not interpolate, substitute another timestamp,
or impute a value.
Keep endpoint validity, reference-check eligibility, and method-adherence status distinct. A failed or
incomplete reference check makes the run instrument-ineligible. A documented procedural violation
makes it nonconforming. Insufficient verification of an identity-defining motor requirement makes method
conformity unverified.

- A fixed temperature probe whose sensing tip is 15 ± 1 mm above the internal base and 20 ± 1 mm
horizontally from the shaft axis, without touching the vessel or paddle.
- A probe/logger with 0.1 °C reporting resolution, rated accuracy no worse than ±0.2 °C over 20–50 °C,
and rated 90% response time no longer than five seconds. Its certified measurement range must include
0–60 °C.
- A warming water bath, timer or synchronized controller, ambient thermometer, and a dry cork support
10 ± 1 mm thick.

Command logs and rated motor performance do not themselves measure actual speed, transition
duration, or revolution totals. Without suitable existing feedback, some physical adherence requirements
may remain unverified. No equality of mechanical work or energy input follows from nominal rotation
totals.
A future comparison would require human decisions about allocation, run order, replication, apparatus
reuse, and confounding control. This source specifies none of those study-level decisions and supplies
no sample-size justification.

Reused apparatus, runs conducted in the same session, or shared preparations may introduce
dependence. Within-run temperature samples must not be counted as independent replicates.
Causal conclusions cannot follow from procedural definitions alone. Even future observed differences
would require an appropriate comparison design and examination of alternative explanations. Findings
could not automatically generalize to other volumes, vessels, fluids, stirring geometries, ambient
conditions, or observation durations.

Section 5 — Outcome and scoring
Measured construct: Five-minute temperature drop at the fixed probe location. This is an operational
temperature measure, not a direct measure of total heat lost, energy efficiency, or uniform bulk-water
temperature.
Observation unit: One conforming run with one fresh aliquot.
Observable scoring inputs: The logged initial temperature T0 and the logged temperature T300, both in
degrees Celsius, together with their timestamps, reference-check association, and procedural-validity
record.
Exact derivation rule:
Temperature-drop score S = T0 − T300.
Use the recorded temperatures at their 0.1 °C resolution. Subtract without additional transformation,
normalization, absolute-value conversion, clipping, or averaging.

Commanded versus actual speed: A 30-rpm setting is a command. A display that repeats the setting is
not necessarily a measurement of actual paddle speed. Record whether any available speed feedback is
measured, controller-estimated, or merely the commanded setting.
Schedule boundaries: The start command must follow T0 and occur within one second of time zero.
The stop command has a nominal boundary of 300 seconds, must occur within one second of that
boundary, and must follow capture of T300.

Transition allowance: The existing one-second transition allowance is the maximum physical transition
duration from an issued command to its corresponding state: speed within ±2 rpm of the target after a
start command, or stationary paddle after a stop command. It is separate from the command-boundary
timing allowance. One allowance must not be reported as verification of the other.
Acceleration and deceleration mean that physical motion need not coincide exactly with the nominal
active interval. Brief post-command deceleration is a transition, not an additional scheduled stirring
interval.

Experimental and observation unit: One fresh water aliquot undergoing one uninterrupted five-minute
run with one stirring method. Temperature samples within a run are repeated measurements of that unit,
not independent experimental units.
Necessary materials and apparatus:
- An open, straight-sided cylindrical borosilicate glass vessel with internal diameter 70 ± 2 mm, wall
thickness 2 ± 0.5 mm, and capacity sufficient for 100 mL without overflow.
- 100 ± 1 mL of deionized water per run, measured with a graduated cylinder.
- An overhead stirrer with a vertical central shaft and one rectangular stainless-steel paddle, 20 ± 1 mm
wide and 10 ± 1 mm high. The paddle’s lower edge is fixed 5 ± 1 mm above the vessel’s internal base.

1. Under the specified conditions, does the distribution of five-minute fixed-location temperature-drop
scores differ between continuous lower-speed stirring and intermittent higher-speed stirring?
2. How repeatable is the defined score across independently prepared fresh aliquots using each method?
These questions are unresolved within this document. They are not approved Research Gaps or selected
Hypotheses. No preferred direction, expected result, significance claim, or global novelty claim is
supplied.

Section 6 — Assumptions
Case-defining stipulations: The specified water volume, apparatus geometry, initial-temperature
window, environment, timing, stirring schedules, probe location, and score rule define this proposed
case. They are design choices, not experimental discoveries.
Assumptions requiring empirical confirmation:
- The chosen probe and logging arrangement can resolve temperature changes relevant to this
comparison.
- The preparation procedure produces sufficiently comparable initial thermal conditions, including vessel
temperature.
- The commanded stirring schedules can be reproduced within their stated tolerances.
- Differences between repeated preparations and environmental conditions can be documented
sufficiently for a meaningful comparison.

Section 3 — Method A: Continuous low-speed paddle stirring
Method A is continuous clockwise paddle stirring at a commanded speed of 30 revolutions per minute
throughout the nominal interval from time zero to 300 seconds.
It requires the water, vessel, paddle, probe placement, preparation, reference-check eligibility, and
environment defined in Section 2. The paddle remains immersed and is not repositioned during the run.
Start the motor immediately after recording T0; stop it only after recording T300.
The speed setting, uninterrupted operation, direction, geometry, and five-minute duration define Method
A. The nominal schedule specifies 150 paddle revolutions by integrating the commanded speed over the
nominal interval. This is schedule arithmetic, not an observed revolution count.

gap.title: Unresolved score-distribution comparison in the supplied synthetic stirring protocol
gap.description: The source-defined question compares the distributions of five-minute fixed-location temperature-drop scores under continuous lower-speed stirring versus intermittent higher-speed stirring. This comparison remains unresolved within the supplied synthetic procedural document.
gap.why_it_matters: This candidate restates an existing unresolved question. Its potential usefulness is as a research-design direction for human consideration within the supplied synthetic protocol, rather than proof of a newly discovered scientific gap.
assumptions: Implementability of the procedural specifications is an unverified planning assumption, not a source-established fact.

hypothesis.statement: Synthetic workflow demonstration conjecture, not an empirical finding: under the stated hypothetical model, the full distributions of recorded five-minute fixed-location temperature-drop scores for continuous lower-speed stirring and intermittent higher-speed stirring, conditional on jointly valid two-run blocks, have W1 distance greater than delta_demo=1 score °C. This is a nondirectional illustrative-threshold claim; it asserts no superiority, physical mechanism or scientifically justified meaningfulness.
hypothesis.rationale: The cited source identifies the full score-distribution comparison between the two named methods as unresolved. It motivates this demonstration conjecture but does not establish the prediction. The human-proposed purpose is to demonstrate the provenance-preserving, human-gated workflow and support/contradiction/inconclusive logic. The illustrative threshold and mathematical model are demonstration choices, not practical equivalence, a minimum important difference, resolution-derived significance or evidence-based relevance. This qualified operational illustration does not resolve the unrestricted original question or establish a real physical effect.
hypothesis.independent_variable: Compound source-named method labels: continuous lower-speed stirring (A) versus intermittent higher-speed stirring (B). Both speed and schedule remain in the contrast; no causal claim about intermittency alone is made. Labels in the hypothetical model do not verify actual method implementation.
hypothesis.dependent_variable: The entire conditional recorded-score distributions F_A(s)=Pr(S_A<=s|C=1,Q_demo) and F_B(s)=Pr(S_B<=s|C=1,Q_demo), in score °C. C=1 denotes a jointly valid two-run block. Compare them using W1=integral |F_A(s)-F_B(s)| ds over the assumed model domain. This is not a mean-only comparison, a distribution of paired differences, latent physical temperature, heat loss or energy efficiency.
control_variables: For the mathematical demonstration only, retain the same scalar five-minute fixed-location recorded-score interpretation and one score per hypothetical run-record unit; do not normalize, take absolute values, clip or average scores.

Use one fixed hypothetical joint sampling law Q_demo and fixed within-block validity-indicator rules across all attempted blocks; no real apparatus, operator, preparation, environment or measurement performance is specified or certified.

Use the fixed assumed demonstration-model score domain [-15.2,45.2] score °C, fixed illustrative threshold 1 score °C, total alpha=0.05, h=0.5 score °C and one terminal analysis after N_demo=150000 attempted blocks.
hypothesis.falsification_condition: Demonstration rule only: after the fixed N_demo=150000 attempted blocks, let m be the complete jointly valid count. Failed model/record-validity gates, absent inputs or m<127891 leave the claim inconclusive. Otherwise form both empirical CDFs from the m valid scores per arm. With R=60.4 score °C and alpha_A=alpha_B=0.025, use epsilon_j=min(1,sqrt(ln(2/alpha_j)/(2m))), D_hat=integral |Fhat_A-Fhat_B| ds, E=min(R,R*(epsilon_A+epsilon_B)), L=max(0,D_hat-E), U=min(R,D_hat+E). Under the stipulated iid-block and bounded-score assumptions, the one-arm DKWM bounds plus a union bound give interval coverage at least 0.95. Support this illustrative-threshold claim when L>1 score °C; contradict it when U<=1 score °C; otherwise report inconclusive, including L=1<U. U=1 is on the contradiction side. A model-domain violation invalidates the demonstration rather than instructing exclusion of real observations. An invalid gate is not falsification, and non-rejection is not equality. Contradiction concerns W1>1 in this hypothetical conditional model, not exact equality or resolution of the unrestricted original research question. Do not extend the attempted count, switch metrics or use an outcome-selected interval rule.
assumptions: All numeric parameters, model bounds, sampling assumptions and inference rules in this revision are proposed human demonstration design choices. delta_demo=1 score °C is arbitrary and illustrative; it has no claimed scientific or practical meaningfulness.

Q_demo is a hypothetical fixed joint probability law for two source-named run-record units, allocation/order and binary per-run record-validity indicators. Attempted block tuples are independent and identically distributed under that law; scores and validity may be dependent within a block.

Each block contains two distinct hypothetical fresh-aliquot run-record units, one allocated to each method label. Randomly assign unit identities to A/B and independently choose AB or BA order with probability 1/2, independently across blocks. These are model assumptions, not verified real sampling or causal identification.

The two binary record-validity indicators represent stipulated endpoint-valid, instrument-eligible and method-conforming status within the hypothetical model, not results of physical verification. Fixed per-block rules define C=1 exactly when both indicators are 1. The fixed joint-valid probability satisfies 0<p<1; its numeric value is not needed by the conditional rule and no perfect-yield or attainment guarantee is assumed.

All jointly valid model scores are finite and belong to the assumed illustrative domain [-15.2,45.2] score °C, whose width is 60.4 score °C. This is an assumed demonstration-model bound, not current canonical source authority, verified physical support, an approved physical endpoint rule or an instruction to filter real observations.

N_demo=150000 is an arbitrary fixed attempted-block count for arithmetic illustration, not a recommended or approved laboratory workload. The information gate requires 127891 complete jointly valid blocks, hence that many scores per arm. Incomplete blocks remain recorded but do not enter the conditional target; insufficient complete count remains inconclusive.

The planning target is h=delta_demo/2=0.5 score °C. The sufficient complete count is ceil(8*(60.4)^2*ln(80)/(1)^2)=127891 under total alpha=0.05 and equal arm split. This is precision, not power; no actual observations, yield, independent preparations or resource feasibility are established.

The claim is conditional on model validity only. No real Q, apparatus identity, instrument performance, physical conformity, empirical independence, preferred effect direction, superiority or global novelty is established. The joint-valid target does not identify an all-assigned-run or causal effect; the earlier meaningful-design references and their unresolved requirements remain historical and unchanged.
